A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, equations, Table 1, Algorithms 1–3, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports algorithms, regret bounds, counterexamples, and proofs, including in its appendices. It contains no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v5 remains entirely theoretical. Its new general-capacity application derives regret bounds analytically and reports no empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: New Section 4 adds a reduction for capacity decisions: replace arm a by n_a identical-reward copies, organize the copies into cliques, and apply OSMD-G. This is a limited input adaptation; Algorithms 1–3 themselves are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks in empirical training or evaluation. The general-capacity problem added in v5 is studied theoretically.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated experimental comparators. Section 4 adds an analytical comparison with the bound attributed to ABL14, rather than an empirical baseline evaluation.

E3.justification: There are no experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics, or training budgets in either version. The revised theorem assumption concerns theoretical applicability.

E4.justification: No empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses are added. The negative-correlation counterexamples and general-decision-subset analyses are retained, with section renumbering.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, or empirical uncertainty estimates. The theoretical probability guarantees in Appendix D and the concentration lemma in Appendix F are unchanged.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains measured performance results, and Table 1 retains identical regret-rate entries. The newly derived capacity bounds are theoretical additions assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds a capacity decision set and derives regret bounds through the existing graph-feedback theorem. Theorem 1.2 changes S < K to S ≤ K/2, with an explanation added in Appendix A. Section 5.3 corrects Δmin from the best-versus-second-best arm gap to the best-versus-second-best decision gap. These are a derived application and localized corrections; the principal bounds and remaining proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and Section 1.2 add the general-capacity formulation and its improved regret bound as an additional contribution. The original minimax-rate and negative-correlation claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly interprets graph feedback as handling heterogeneous resource capacities without changing the stated regret scaling, discusses time-varying capacities, and qualifies near-optimality through the presence of many unit-capacity arms. Existing mechanism explanations and open problems are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: The algorithm pseudocode and learning-rate and truncation formulas are unchanged. No implementation settings, hardware information, runtime measurements, or code/data access information are added.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work section retain the same works. New Section 4 adds positioning against ABL14: directly applying its semi-bandit bound to replicated arms depends on total capacity, whereas exploiting the clique feedback gives the stated tighter bound.

P1.justification: v5 inserts a short Section 4, expands the abstract and contribution list, and renumbers the former Section 4 as Section 5. It also removes the stray '(author?)' text and updates cross-references. Most prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: Added text changes pagination and moves Algorithm 1 lower on page 7. Table 1 and all three algorithm displays retain their content and structure; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Restricting Theorem 1.2 to S ≤ K/2 and explaining that restriction in Appendix A improves the precision of the existing guarantee. Correcting the decision-gap definition also helps. The new capacity application adds useful scope, although its action-set notation excludes zero under Section 1.3's definition of [n], conflicting with its intended reduction. This local defect limits the gain.
